transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I'm here because... well, work has been difficult lately. I'm a nurse, and it's just... I get distracted a lot. Like, I'll be working on a patient flow issue, and then an IV pump will beep, or a call light goes off, or someone just asks a question nearby. And then I just... I lose my train of thought. Completely forget what I was doing. It happens constantly.
Were you this easily distracted as a child?

I guess so, yeah. Um... even back in elementary school, my teachers used to write that I was... bright, but careless. I was always losing worksheets. Or I'd just forget to turn my homework in. My mom actually had to... she had to sit with me every night just to keep me on track with things.
Do these attention problems also affect you outside of work?

Yeah... I suppose so. Just with routine things, mostly. Like... forgetting to call a family member back. Or paying a bill at home. Um... sometimes I just don't show up for an appointment. I mean to go, and I'll even set a reminder for it, but... I still forget. It just happens.
Do you often feel restless, like you need to keep moving or have trouble sitting still?
No, not really. I mean... I can sit still fine. It's more just... my mind wandering, not my body.
When your concentration gets worse, is that usually only when you’re feeling down or depressed?
Um... no, I don't think so. It's just kind of... an everyday thing. I haven't really noticed it being tied to feeling down.
